claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for release based on aggregate readiness evidence and general risk-management guidance, despite an unresolved small-business onboarding performance gap and without admissible evidence of required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
decision_criteria: If a weakness affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, treat it as material.
For a material limitation, require either resolution before launch, disclosure before launch, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Do not treat product labels such as non-core or low-volume as sufficient to defeat materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
Aggregate readiness evidence can support launch quality, but it does not satisfy a separate policy disclosure requirement.
evidence_requests: Provide the finalized legal determination on whether the small-business onboarding gap must be disclosed.
Provide the actual launch disclosure or model-card language covering this limitation, if it exists.
Provide approved risk-acceptance documentation authorizing launch with this unresolved material limitation.
Provide evidence that the named paid pilot commitments do not make this segment a contractual or named launch use case, if that is being asserted.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the affected small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy threshold.
The release policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations in named launch use cases.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance.
There is no admissible evidence that the material limitation has been disclosed.
Legal review is still open, which the policy text says does not resolve materiality.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not cure the separate disclosure predicate.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification is adequately supported by aggregate readiness evidence alone.
The claim that continued monitoring and documentation are sufficient substitutes for disclosure or approved risk acceptance under the governing policy.
Any implication that the affected segment is immaterial because it is described as non-core or low-volume.
